decisive_items: Methenamine silver staining revealed yeast-like structures associated with septate hyphae demonstrating acute-angle branching.
Chest CT (lung window) showed cavitary and noncavitary nodules and masses with faint surrounding ground-glass opacity (“halo sign”)
Histopathologic analysis showed diffuse necrotizing granulomatous inflammation and fungal elements.
response.rationale: The acute-angle branching septate hyphae are pathognomonic for Aspergillus, distinguishing it from histoplasmosis (yeast forms without septate hyphae) and mucormycosis (broad, non-septate hyphae with right-angle branching). The halo sign and necrotizing granulomas further support invasive aspergillosis.

rejected.why: Histoplasmosis would show yeast-like organisms without septate hyphae; the acute-angle branching septate hyphae contradict this.
Mucormycosis has broad, non-septate hyphae with right-angle branching, not the described septate acute-angle morphology.
